classification.habit: Small, much-branched, thorny shrub or small tree, 1.2–1.8 m tall.
classification.habitat: Arid rocky tracts and dry hills.
classification.distribution: Rajasthan, Gujarat (Kutch), Madhya Pradesh and Karnataka; now a threatened species.

identification.description: Irregular brownish-yellow translucent or sticky oleo-gum resin masses with strong balsamic aromatic odor.
identification.whole_plant: Thorny shrub with knotty crooked branches, ash-coloured papery bark and small trifoliate leaves.
identification.stem: Branches knotty, crooked, ending in sharp spines.
identification.leaf: Small, 1–3-foliolate, leaflets obovate, serrate towards the tip, shining.
identification.fruit: Ovoid drupe, red when ripe, about 1 cm long.
identification.bark: Ash-coloured, peeling in papery flakes; exudes the aromatic oleo-gum resin when incised.
identification_points: Vermicular or stalactitic pale yellow to brown pieces
Forms milky emulsion in hot water
Bitter, astringent taste; sticky when fresh

dosha.pitta: may increase; use according to context

therapeutics.anupana: Ushnodaka (warm water); specific anupanas such as Rasnadi kwatha in Vatavyadhi.
therapeutics.precautions: Use only shodhita guggulu (e.g. boiled in Triphala kwatha or cow's milk). Can cause gastric upset, skin rash and loose stools; may interact with anticoagulants, thyroid drugs and propranolol. Fresh guggulu is brimhana and old guggulu lekhana.
therapeutics.contraindications: Contraindicated in pregnancy; avoid in Pitta-predominant conditions, bleeding disorders and during menstruation in heavy bleeders. Classical apathya includes sour foods, excessive exertion, sun and anger during its use.

shlokas:
गुग्गुलुर्विशदस्तिक्तो वीर्योष्णः पित्तलः सरः ।
कषायः कटुकः पाके कटू रूक्षो लघुः परः ॥३५॥
nighantu_references: Bhavaprakasha Nighantu, Karpuradi Varga. The searchable recension places Guggulu after the five varieties (verses 29–30) and its properties in the following verses; exact verse numbering is edition-dependent. The unverified 33–35 citation is removed.

phytochemistry.chemical_notes: The oleo-gum resin contains essential oil, gum and resin, with the pregnane steroids guggulsterone E and Z as the main bioactive markers.

modern_information.evidence_summary: Excellent for arthritis, high cholesterol, and detoxification.
modern_information.safety_notes: Generally tolerated as shodhita guggulu; adverse effects include gastric upset, headache and skin rash, and it may interact with several prescription drugs.
